A1.justification: Both 27-page PDFs describe RLZero and include readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. Corresponding material can be matched despite repagination and an added appendix experiment.

before.justification: v2 reports original continuous-control experiments, including language-to-behavior and cross-embodiment evaluations, quantitative returns, win rates, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a comparison of Forward-Backward and Proto Successor Measures behavior foundation models.

M1.justification: The imagine–project–imitate pipeline, default Forward-Backward model, and closed-form inference remain unchanged. Proto Successor Measures is tested as an alternative compatible BFM in an ablation; the proposed framework is not revised.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 25 language-to-behavior tasks and 17 cross-embodiment tasks. The new BFM ablation reuses 19 existing Walker, Quadruped, and Cheetah tasks without expanding coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds RLZero using Proto Successor Measures as a comparator against the Forward-Backward implementation in Table 8. The existing IQL, TD3, GenRL, SMODICE, and other ablation comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.5 adds an experimental control that varies BFM training between PSM and FB on 19 retained tasks, using the existing GPT-4o win-rate evaluation against TD3 plus image-language rewards. Previously reported protocols and FB settings remain unchanged; PSM-specific training budgets are not supplied.

E4.justification: The new Appendix C.5 and Table 8 test sensitivity to the choice of BFM training algorithm. Existing discriminator, imagination-free, failure-case, and video-embedding analyses remain present.

E5.justification: Five-seed evaluations, existing ± reporting, and the Mann–Whitney U test at significance level 0.05 are retained. The new ablation uses the established wins-out-of-five reporting style without adding statistical procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports PSM results for 19 tasks, averaging 71.6% wins against the TD3 baseline, alongside 84.2% for FB. The matched FB task scores and existing benchmark results are unchanged. The 84.2% subset average is not an improvement over the retained 25-task average of 83.2%; v2 Table 8 also remains numerically unchanged as v3 Table 9.

T1.justification: The successor-measure definitions, distribution-matching formulation, Theorem 1, and Appendix A proof retain their mathematical content. Equation differences are typesetting changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of direct policy inference without in-domain supervision or test-time gradient updates, including cross-embodiment imitation. The added ablation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The discussions of generation failures, prompt sensitivity, background distractors, approximate symmetries, and unreliable embedding-similarity evaluation are retained. The new PSM paragraph reports comparative performance without adding a mechanism explanation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: The project-page link beneath v2's abstract is removed from v3, reducing access information supplied by the paper. Existing implementation links, hardware information, and FB hyperparameters remain; no PSM-specific implementation settings are added.

R1.justification: The cited-work membership and related-work positioning remain unchanged. The PSM reference changes from its preprint title to its ICML publication title and is renumbered; it is the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations and acknowledgments, removes the Author Contributions section, and inserts Appendix C.5 while retaining nearly all scientific prose. Section 4.3 incorrectly changes its discriminator-comparison reference from C.2 to C.5, although that comparison remains in C.2.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 8, renumbers the previous Table 8 as Table 9, and repositions existing figures and tables through reflow. Conference formatting and the Table 2 caption also change. Existing figure content is retained, with identical embedded image data.

improvement.justification: v2 lacks a direct FB-versus-PSM comparison; v3's Appendix C.5 and Table 8 provide useful evidence about sensitivity to this implementation choice across 19 existing tasks. This modest empirical benefit is limited by missing PSM-specific settings and tempered by the removed project link and incorrect appendix reference. The main scientific results and claims remain stable.
